title: AI DIDN’T FIND THE HOLY GRAIL — BUT IT DID KILL MY COOLING FAN.
author: EAForexLab
selftext:
For the past few days, my AI agent has been optimizing trading strategies in MetaTrader 5 almost nonstop. Thousands of backtests using real tick data, with the CPU running under heavy load the entire time.

Then today, my laptop started making some very strange noises. Sounded like it was getting ready for takeoff.

We opened it up, cleaned everything out… no luck. Looks like the cooling fan has officially decided to retire. Now I'm waiting for a replacement.

The funniest part? AI still hasn't found me the Holy Grail of trading, but it apparently managed to finish off my cooling fan.

If there's one lesson here, it's that heavy optimization jobs are better off running on a remote server with enough computing power. And for serious MT5 optimization, a cheap VPS probably won't cut it. You need something with real horsepower.

Turns out AI-powered trading automation has some hidden costs. 😅

comments.author: cavityfilla
comments.body: Businesses implementing AI through OpenAI and Anthropic and other AI providers are also figuring this out. Bulk company laptops issued in previous IT renewal cycles just don’t cut it. Businesses are also waking up to the additional hardware costs of AI

comments.author: spoidercide
comments.body:
Glad I scooped up my 7800x3d + 9070xt 32gb ddr5 combo at the beginning of the year for a steal price. It's easily worth 50-100% more what I paid for it now.

It's gone from being a gaming machine to a quantitative finance strategy engine xD

Find a budget friendly solution to your quantitative goals.

Your mistake was trying to find a holy grail through individual strategies...

With the right engine and an AI portfolio aggregator you can net out several strategies ran in an aggregate portfolio which is the only grail of quant finance:

Rotating in and out paramater adjusted individual strategies for an aggregate portfolio performance.

You don't need 1 incredible strategy (doesn't exist and when you size up, your portfolio feels the losing days as well)

You just need a bunch of decent strategies that when sized together the equity curve is nice and smooth and makes the same return as that "holy grail" but with a much smoother equity curve and much less exposure to the market.
